Ruśama is mentioned three times in the Rigveda as a protégé of indra. The Ruśamas occur in another passage of the Rigveda with their generous king ṛṇaṃcaya; they are also referred to, with their king kaurama, in a passage of the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes viii. 3, 13; 4, 2; 51, 9.

Ruśamā is mentioned in the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa (xxv. 13, 3), where she is said to have run round kurukṣetra, and so to have defeated indra, who understood her challenge to refer to the earth proper. The story indicates the connexion of the Ruśamas with the Kurus.

Ruṣatī in one passage of the Rigveda denotes, according to Ludwig, a maiden who was married to śyāva. On the other hand, Roth treats the word as ruśatī, ‘white,’ and ruśatīm seems clearly to be the reading of the text. It is doubtful what the meaning is, and whether śyāva is a proper name at all.
Foot notes i. 117, 8.
